examples.en: These days I eat multigrain rice every morning.
Multigrain rice is a bit coarser than white rice.
I ate multigrain rice with seasoned vegetable side dishes.
I switched because they say multigrain rice is good for health.
Please give me multigrain rice, not white rice.
Does this restaurant offer multigrain rice too?

explain: 쌀에 보리, 콩, 수수 같은 여러 곡식을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 보리만 섞으면 '보리밥', 현미로 지으면 '현미밥'이라고 따로 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: I made multigrain rice on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥을 짓다'와 같이 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase, like '밥을 짓다'.

phrases.en: Multigrain rice is good for you, so I eat it often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강을 이유로 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when giving health as a reason.

phrases.en: I eat multigrain rice instead of white rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흰밥과 비교해서 선택을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a choice compared with white rice.

explain_en: It is rice cooked with a mix of grains such as barley, beans and sorghum. If only barley is mixed in it is called '보리밥', and rice made with brown rice is '현미밥'.

examples.en: Pine nut porridge is soft and good when you are sick.
I bought a bag of pine nuts at the supermarket.
Pine nuts are floating on the sujeonggwa.
I got a snack made of pine nuts as a gift.
I sprinkled a handful of pine nuts on the salad.
Pine nuts are nutty but expensive.

explain: 잣은 잣나무의 씨앗이라 고소하고 값이 비싼 편이에요. 잣죽, 수정과, 한과처럼 한국 음식에 자주 들어가고, 음식 위에 올리는 고명으로도 많이 써요. 호두보다 훨씬 작고 부드러워요.

phrases.en: I put pine nuts in the cinnamon punch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 재료로 더할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adding pine nuts as an ingredient.

phrases.en: I put pine nuts on top of the rice cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고명으로 음식 위에 얹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when topping a dish as a garnish.

phrases.en: There are many Korean pine trees in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잣이 열리는 나무를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The tree that produces pine nuts.

explain_en: Pine nuts are the seeds of the Korean pine, rich in flavor and rather expensive. They go into Korean dishes such as 잣죽, 수정과 and 한과, and are often used as a garnish called 고명. They are much smaller and softer than 호두 (walnuts).

examples.en: The meat is sizzling in the pan.
I like the sound of pork belly sizzling.
Turn down the heat when the oil starts to sizzle.
The frying pan sizzled and a delicious smell came out.
The sausage sizzled on the hot griddle.
The sizzling sound had stopped before I knew it.

explain: 뜨거운 기름이나 불판에서 고기, 전이 익을 때 나는 소리를 나타내서 영어로는 sizzle에 가까워요. 같은 소리를 '지글지글'이라고도 해요. '보글보글'은 찌개처럼 국물이 끓는 소리라서 달라요.

phrases.en: I can hear the sound of oil sizzling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로 써서 소리를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a sound before a noun.

phrases.en: The pancake is cooking with a sizzle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)며'로 이어서 익는 모습과 소리를 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linking with -(으)며 shows the cooking and the sound together.

phrases.en: A sizzling sound comes from the grill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지글거리다'와 같은 소리를 부사 '지글지글'로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the adverb 지글지글 for the same sound.

explain_en: It describes the sound of meat or pancakes cooking on hot oil or a griddle, closer to English 'sizzle'. The sound word '지글지글' is the same thing. '보글보글' is different: it is the bubbling of a stew or soup.

t90.ax: The meat is sizzling in the pan.

examples.en: I looked across through the window at the house opposite.

examples.ko: 강 건너편 마을을 건너다보니 불빛이 반짝여요.
examples.en: Looking across at the village on the other side of the river, lights sparkle.

examples.ko: 친구가 길 건너에서 이쪽을 건너다보고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is looking this way from across the road.

examples.ko: 아이가 창가에 서서 강 건너편 산을 건너다봐요.
examples.en: The child stands by the window and looks across the river at the mountain.

examples.ko: 건너다보면 바다 쪽에 작은 섬이 보여요.
examples.en: If you look across, you can see a small island near the sea.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말없이 저를 건너다보기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just looked across at me without saying a word.

explain: 멀리 떨어진 맞은편을 바라볼 때 써요. 위쪽을 향해 보는 '쳐다보다'와 달라요. 담이나 울타리 너머로 보는 건 '넘겨다보다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child is looking across the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 맞은편을 보고 있는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of looking across right now.

phrases.en: I can see the sea across from the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞은편이 눈에 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the far side is visible.

phrases.en: I looked across at the house opposite.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞은편'과 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with 맞은편.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at the opposite side

explain_en: You use it when looking at something far away on the opposite side. It is different from '쳐다보다', which means looking up at something. Looking over a wall or fence is '넘겨다보다'.

examples.en: I walked through every alley of Seoul taking photos.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 골목골목마다 작은 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has a small shop in every alley.
The delivery driver knows every alley.
A delicious smell comes from every alley.
I want to wander around every nook and alley.

examples.ko: 골목골목 불이 켜지니 동네가 아늑해 보여요.
examples.en: With the lights on in every alley, the neighborhood looks cozy.

explain: '골목'을 겹쳐서 이 골목 저 골목 전부라는 느낌을 줘요. '마다'나 '을/에서'와 자주 쓰고, '곳곳', '구석구석'과 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: There are pretty cafes in every alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마다'를 붙이면 빠짐없이 모든 골목이라는 뜻이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '마다' strengthens the sense of 'every single alley'.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 시장 골목골목을 누비며 구경했어요.
phrases.en: I wandered through every alley of the market all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '누비다'는 여기저기 다닌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '누비다' means to go all around.

phrases.en: There are parks all over the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골목골목'보다 범위가 넓어서 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It covers a wider range than '골목골목' and fits any place.

explain_en: Doubling '골목' gives the feel of this alley, that alley, all of them. It is often used with '마다', '을' or '에서', and feels similar to '곳곳' or '구석구석'.

examples.en: A monument stands in the middle of the square.
I took photos with friends in front of the monument.

examples.ko: 이 기념탑은 오래전 일을 기억하려고 세웠어요.
examples.en: This monument was built to remember something from long ago.
There's also a small monument at the entrance of the village.
I went early in the morning to see the monument.
The area around the monument is neatly kept.

explain: 어떤 일이나 사람을 기억하려고 탑 모양으로 높이 세운 것을 말해요. 비슷한 '기념비'는 비석 모양이라서 모양이 달라요. '기념탑을 세우다, 기념탑이 서 있다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The villagers built a monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억하려고 새로 만들 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase for building one to remember something.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 잘 띄어서 약속 장소로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easy to spot, so it is often used as a meeting place.

phrases.en: I went to see the monument on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 가는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the purpose of going to see it.

explain_en: It is a tall structure shaped like a tower, built to remember an event or person. The similar '기념비' is a stone-tablet type, so the shape differs. You say '기념탑을 세우다' or '기념탑이 서 있다'.

t90.ax: The area around the monument is neatly kept.

examples.ko: 마당 수돗가에서 아이들이 손을 씻고 있어요.
examples.en: The kids are washing their hands at the outdoor tap in the yard.

examples.ko: 시골집 수돗가에서 빨래를 했던 기억이 나요.
examples.en: I remember doing laundry at the tap of our country house.
The tap area on the playground is crowded every lunch break.
Water has spilled around the tap, so the floor is slippery.
After coming down from the hike, I washed my shoes at the tap.
There is a small flower bed next to the tap.

explain: 집 마당, 학교 운동장, 공원처럼 야외에 수도꼭지가 있는 곳을 말해서, 실내의 '싱크대'나 '세면대'와는 달라요. 사이시옷이 들어가서 '수돗가'라고 써요.

phrases.en: I washed my shoes at the outdoor tap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야외에서 물로 씻을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for washing with water outdoors.

phrases.en: There is a small flower bed next to the outdoor tap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '옆'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '옆' to describe location.

phrases.en: I drank water at the tap on the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 자주 보는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names a place commonly seen at schools.

explain_en: It refers to the spot with a tap outdoors, such as a yard, a school playground or a park, unlike an indoor '싱크대' (sink) or '세면대' (washbasin). It is written with a sai-siot, as '수돗가'.

examples.en: A patrol car is parked in front of the police substation.
A patrol car goes around our neighborhood every night.

examples.ko: 순찰차를 보면 운전을 더 조심하게 돼요.
examples.en: When I see a patrol car, I drive more carefully.

examples.ko: 순찰차 한 대가 사이렌을 켜고 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A patrol car passed by with its siren on.
The police officer got out of the patrol car and asked me for directions.

examples.ko: 아파트 입구에 순찰차가 있어서 마음이 놓여요.
examples.en: There is a patrol car at the apartment entrance, so I feel safe.

explain: 일상에서는 '경찰차'라고도 많이 말해요. 순찰차는 동네를 돌며 살피는 차라는 느낌이 있어서 '순찰차가 돌다', '순찰차를 보다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A police car is at the scene of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '경찰차'라고도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people also say 경찰차 a lot.

phrases.en: A patrol car goes around the alley every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동네를 돌며 살피는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a car going around and watching over a neighborhood.
phrases.en_equiv: a patrol car makes its rounds

phrases.en: I feel safe when I see a patrol car on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 마주친 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for seeing one on the road.

explain_en: In daily talk people also say '경찰차' (police car). 순찰차 carries the feel of a car that goes around an area keeping watch, so phrases like '순찰차가 돌다' (a patrol car makes its rounds) are common.

examples.en: His excuse was quite convincing.
I came up with a plausible excuse and skipped the appointment.
In the photo, the food looks decent.

examples.ko: 소문을 더 그럴듯하게 만들려고 숫자까지 지어낸 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: Someone even made up numbers to make the rumor more believable.
There are many stories that sound plausible but aren't true.
In a hanbok, you look quite the part.

explain: 진짜처럼 믿을 만하거나 꽤 괜찮아 보일 때 써요. 말이 그럴듯하다고 하면 사실은 아닐 수도 있다는 의심이 살짝 들어가요. 반대로 '제법 그럴듯하네요'처럼 칭찬으로도 써요.

phrases.en: This plan looks quite plausible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉보기에 괜찮고 믿을 만하다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks reasonable or believable.

phrases.en: I decorated the room to look nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제법 멋지게 보이도록 만들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it was made to look quite decent.

phrases.en: That reason doesn't sound very convincing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기 어렵다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is hard to believe.

explain_en: Use it for something that seems believable or looks quite decent. Calling an account 그럴듯하다 can hint at slight doubt that it's actually true. It can also be praise, as in '제법 그럴듯하네요'.

examples.en: I'm sweating, so my body feels sticky.
Natto has long sticky strands that stretch out.
The candy melted and my hands were sticky.
The sticky dough clung to my hands.

examples.ko: 이 풀은 너무 끈적끈적해서 쓰기 불편해요.
examples.en: This glue is so sticky that it's hard to use.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 방 안 공기도 끈적끈적하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: During the rainy season, even the air in the room feels sticky.

explain: '끈적끈적한 반죽'처럼 명사 앞에서 쓰거나 몸의 느낌을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '끈끈하다'도 비슷한데, '끈끈한 우정'처럼 사람 사이의 관계가 깊을 때도 쓰는 점이 달라요. 끈적끈적하다는 보통 느낌이 좋지 않을 때 써요.

phrases.en: I spilled juice, so I washed my sticky hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, the verb changes to the '-ㄴ' modifier form.

phrases.en: In summer it's hot, so my skin feels sticky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 물건의 지금 느낌을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite present form for describing how something or your body feels right now.

phrases.en: This lotion is not sticky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈적이는 느낌이 없어서 좋다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say something is pleasantly not sticky.

explain_en: It is natural before a noun, as in '끈적끈적한 반죽', or when describing how your body feels. '끈끈하다' is similar, but it can also describe close relationships, as in '끈끈한 우정'. '끈적끈적하다' usually carries an unpleasant feeling.

t90.ax: The sticky dough clung to my hands.

en: to be wonderful; to be great

examples.en: The kimchi stew at this place is fantastic.
The concert I saw yesterday was really amazing.
I found a café with a stunning view.
Your singing is amazing!

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 '날씨 한번 끝내주네'라고 하면 반어법이에요.
examples.en: Saying 'What great weather!' on a rainy day is sarcasm.

examples.ko: 여행 계획이 끝내주게 짜여서 모두 좋아했어요.
examples.en: The travel plan was put together so well that everyone loved it.

explain: '아주 훌륭하다', '최고다'라는 뜻으로 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 구어체예요. 어른이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '훌륭해요', '최고예요'가 더 어울려요. 반어법으로 비꼬아 쓰기도 해서 말투를 잘 봐야 해요.

phrases.example: 이 집 갈비는 정말 끝내주는 맛이에요.
phrases.en: This place's ribs taste absolutely amazing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '-는'을 붙여 '최고의'라는 뜻으로 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun with '-는', it means 'fantastic'.

phrases.en: Wow, the view here is amazing!
phrases.nuance_ko: 보고 느낀 감탄을 말할 때 '-네요'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-네요' expresses admiration at something you just noticed.

phrases.en: This song is really awesome.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구끼리 쓰는 반말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech among close friends.

explain_en: This is a casual spoken word used among friends to say something is excellent or the best. With elders or in formal settings, '훌륭해요' or '최고예요' fits better. It can also be used sarcastically, so pay attention to the tone.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 났는지 무표정으로 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat with a blank face, maybe because he was angry.
The expressionless child suddenly started to laugh.

examples.ko: 사진 속 얼굴이 무표정이라서 기분을 모르겠어요.
examples.en: The face in the photo is blank, so I can't tell the mood.
The interviewers kept a blank expression the whole time.
A person who speaks with a blank face is scarier.
Even after hearing sad news, his face stayed blank.

explain: '무표정으로 서 있다', '무표정을 유지하다'처럼 그 순간의 얼굴 이야기예요. 성격이 말이 없고 딱딱한 사람은 '무뚝뚝하다'라고 해요. '무'는 '없다'는 뜻이라 '무관심', '무소식'에도 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: He kept a blank expression until the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정을 얼굴에 드러내지 않고 버틴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping emotions off your face.

phrases.en: My friend answered with a blank face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때의 얼굴이 아무 느낌 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone speaks with no expression.

phrases.en: My friend has had a blank face all day today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 얼굴 상태를 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to describe someone's face right now.

explain_en: It describes the face at a given moment: 무표정으로 서 있다, 무표정을 유지하다. A reserved, curt personality is 무뚝뚝하다 instead. The 무 means 'none' and also appears in 무관심 and 무소식.

examples.en: As time passed, his true self was revealed.
He took off the mask and showed his true self.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 도시의 본모습을 잘 담았어요.
examples.en: This photo captures the true look of the city well.
In front of my friends, I just stay as my true self.
His real self was surprisingly quiet.

examples.ko: 복원을 하니 옛 성당의 본모습에 가까워졌어요.
examples.en: After the restoration, the old cathedral came closer to its original look.

explain: 꾸미거나 숨기지 않은 원래의 모습을 말해요. 사람의 성격에도 쓰고 장소나 물건의 처음 모양에도 써요. '본모습이 드러나다', '본모습을 보이다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: When he got angry, he showed his true self.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기던 모습이 밖으로 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a hidden side becomes visible.

phrases.en: After the repair, it went back to its original look.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본모습'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word than 본모습.

phrases.en: He hid his true self and pretended to be kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 모습을 일부러 숨길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deliberately hiding one's real self.

explain_en: It is the original appearance or character without any disguise or decoration, used for people's personalities and for the first form of places or things. Common patterns are '본모습이 드러나다' and '본모습을 보이다'.

examples.en: A rainbow is a spectrum of light.
This film covers a wide range of emotions.
That singer has a broad musical range.

examples.ko: 정치 스펙트럼이 다른 사람들과도 대화해 봤어요.
examples.en: I've talked with people from different parts of the political spectrum.

examples.ko: 넓은 스펙트럼의 책을 읽으면 생각도 넓어져요.
examples.en: Reading books across a wide spectrum broadens your thinking too.
We observed a spectrum in science class.

explain: 스펙트럼은 과학에서는 빛을 색깔별로 나눈 띠를 말하고, 일상에서는 '넓은 스펙트럼'처럼 어떤 것이 다룰 수 있는 범위를 비유로 말할 때 써요. '범위'보다 서로 다른 것들이 이어져 있는 폭이라는 느낌이 있어요. 참고로 '스펙'이라는 말은 취업 준비에서 쓰는 '조건'이라서 이 단어와는 달라요.

phrases.example: 이 가수는 넓은 스펙트럼의 음악을 해요.
phrases.en: This singer does music across a wide spectrum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다룰 수 있는 범위가 넓고 다양하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something covers a wide and varied range.

phrases.example: 우리 반 친구들은 생각의 스펙트럼이 다양해요.
phrases.en: My classmates have a wide spectrum of opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 것들이 이어져 있다는 느낌으로, 사람이나 의견의 차이를 말할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests different things lying along a continuum; good for describing differences in people or opinions.

phrases.en: We looked at the spectrum of light in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학에서 빛을 색깔별로 나눈 띠를 말하는 원래 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original scientific meaning: light split into bands of color.

explain_en: Seupekteureom is, in science, a band of light split by colour, and in daily life a figurative range, as in a wide spectrum. It suggests a continuous spread of different things rather than just a 범위. Note that 스펙, used in job hunting for credentials, is a different word.
